title: Unique identifier in geofencing notifications
description: The arrival/departure notification likely contains unique identifiers (e.g., user ID, device ID) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across the system.

title: Quasi-identifier through location and timing
description: Combination of location data (geofence entry/exit) and timestamp can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes data that identifies individuals (arrival/departure notifications tied to specific users or devices).

title: Identifier in notification data
description: The notification data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., user ID, device identifier).

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location data (geofence entry/exit) and timing information are revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject.

title: Observed communications
description: The arrival/departure notification can be observed by unauthorized parties during transmission or at the receiving endpoint.

title: Sensitive location data type
description: Location data is considered highly sensitive personal data and may be collected/processed beyond what is strictly required for the geofencing functionality.

title: Data propagation to external entity
description: Personal data (location notifications) is propagated to an external entity (EE1) where it may be accessible beyond the functional necessity.

title: Data shared with external parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to external parties (EE1) beyond what may be functionally necessary for the geofencing alert functionality.

title: Unawareness of location tracking
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location data (geofence entry/exit) is being collected, processed, and transmitted to external entities.

title: Lack of control over data processing
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is processed and shared with external entities.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the geofencing functionality, potentially violating data minimization requirements.

title: Linking through unique identifier
description: The child's location data can be linked to the child through unique identifiers (e.g., user ID, device ID) that are transmitted with the location information.
assumptions: The system uses identifiers to track the child across sessions and devices.

title: Quasi-identifier combining data
description: Location data combined with other attributes (time, location patterns, family relationships) can serve as quasi-identifiers to uniquely identify the child.
assumptions: Location data is combined with metadata about when and where the child is located.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified personal data (child's location) that directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: The child's location is explicitly identified and processed by the Mobile App Backend.

title: Identifier in data
description: The data contains unique references to the child's identity through location data that can be traced back to the specific child.
assumptions: Location data is associated with the child's identity in the system.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Location data is highly sensitive personal data that reveals the child's movements, routines, and whereabouts, which may be more sensitive than functionally required.
assumptions: Location data is considered sensitive under privacy regulations.

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Location data may be propagated to other services or systems beyond the immediate parent-child guardian relationship where it is not needed.
assumptions: The Mobile App Backend may share data with third-party services or analytics.

title: Dynamic set of parties
description: The parties with whom location data is shared (secondary guardians) are determined dynamically and may change frequently as parents invite different relatives.
assumptions: Parents can add/remove secondary guardians at any time.

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their location data is being shared with secondary guardians beyond the parent.
assumptions: Children may not understand the implications of location sharing with other family members.

title: Lack of control over preferences
description: The child and potentially the parent may lack control over who can access their location data and for how long.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not provide granular control over data sharing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the functional goal of allowing secondary guardians to view the child's location.
assumptions: The system may collect or process more location data than necessary (e.g., historical data, precise coordinates).

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's live location data can be linked to a specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking and association of location data with individual identity.
assumptions: Location data is associated with identifiable user accounts or devices

title: Profiling an individual through location data
description: Live location data can be analyzed to profile a child's movements, routines, and patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily activities and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is collected over time and can be analyzed for patterns

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes identified personal data (child's live location) which directly reveals the identity and whereabouts of the data subject.
assumptions: Location data is tied to identifiable individuals

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Live location is a revealing attribute that can support identification of the data subject and reveal sensitive information about their activities and presence at specific locations.
assumptions: Location data reveals sensitive contextual information

title: Collection of highly sensitive data type
description: Live location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required. Sharing live location with a secondary guardian may exceed functional necessity.
assumptions: Live location is considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Excessive granularity in location data
description: Live location data is of very fine-grained granularity (real-time, continuous), which may be more detailed than needed for the stated purpose of guardian access.
assumptions: Guardian access could be satisfied with less granular location data

title: Data propagation to external party
description: Location data is propagated to an external party (Secondary Guardian) where it may be accessible beyond the immediate functional need, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: External parties may have additional access or use cases for the data

title: Sharing with predetermined external party
description: Location data is shared with a predetermined set of parties (Secondary Guardian) that is known at design time, which may still represent excessive exposure if not strictly necessary.
assumptions: The set of guardians is fixed and known upfront

title: Unawareness of location data processing
description: The child (data subject) may not be fully aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, or may not understand the implications of this sharing.
assumptions: Data subjects may not have complete visibility into data sharing practices

title: Lack of control over location data sharing
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is shared with the secondary guardian, including duration and scope of access.
assumptions: Data subjects need granular control over data sharing preferences

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing live location data with a secondary guardian may process more personal data than actually needed, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies to this processing activity

title: Potential invalid consent for location sharing
description: Location data collection and sharing may not rely on valid consent from the child or their guardians, especially if consent is not properly obtained or documented.
assumptions: Valid consent is required for processing children's location data

title: Quasi-identifier combining in aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., device type, usage patterns, time spent) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individual users when combined with external data.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficiently robust to prevent re-identification
uncertainty_note: Assuming aggregation is not fully anonymized

title: Profiling through analytics data
description: Usage and engagement analytics can be analyzed to create user profiles, linking behavioral patterns to specific individuals and potentially revealing sensitive information about user preferences and habits.
assumptions: Analytics partner may use data for profiling purposes
uncertainty_note: Depends on analytics partner's data usage policies

title: Data propagation to external analytics partner
description: Personal data is propagated to an external advertising/analytics partner (EE4) where it may be accessible beyond the original functional purpose of funding the app's free tier.
assumptions: External partner may have broader access to the data than intended
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard third-party data sharing practices

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined set of external parties (advertising/analytics partner) that may not be functionally necessary for the core app functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a known third party
uncertainty_note: Based on flow description indicating data sharing with EE4

title: User unawareness of data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their usage and engagement analytics are being shared with an external advertising/analytics partner to fund the app's free tier.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into this data sharing

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their usage and engagement data is shared with external analytics partners.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanism for analytics data sharing
uncertainty_note: Depends on app's privacy settings implementation

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (usage and engagement analytics) may be processed and shared than is actually needed to achieve the functional goal of funding the app's free tier.
assumptions: Aggregated analytics may contain more detail than necessary
uncertainty_note: Assuming analytics data is more granular than strictly needed
